terms.gloss: let come or go to a place, let in, admit; give an audience to
evidence: Nep. Eum. 12: vetuit ad eum quemquam admittī (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Att. 13.52: nec quemquam admīsit (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: notārium vocō et diē admissō quae fōrmāveram dictō
phrases.english: I call my secretary and, letting in the daylight, dictate what I have composed
he forbade anyone to be admitted to him

sources: Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections, checked against the editions named there.
